login.signIn: Sign in to Capy in the app with the capy.ai account of the ademark user (Google, GitHub or email); the Mac pairs as a device on first sign-in.

openProject.goal: Above the composer are two selectors: the project (left; it reads a project name such as ClickVids) and where the thread runs (right; it reads 'Cloud' or the name of this Mac). Make the project selector read 'capy' and the run selector read this Mac, with the project's folder on this Mac being ${worktree}. Steps: click the project selector, type capy in 'Search projects', and click a project named capy in the list (Enter does not pick it). Then click the run selector and choose the row that says 'This Mac'. If a box 'Set up capy on this Mac' shows, click 'Choose folder'. That opens a macOS file dialog (with Cancel and Open buttons): never click inside that dialog, use only keys there: press cmd+shift+g, type ${worktree}, press enter, wait one second, and press enter again; the dialog then closes. If instead a path field inside Capy shows (with 'Select' at its bottom), press cmd+a, type ${worktree}, and press cmd+enter. If no project named capy is in the list, click 'New project', then 'Folder on a machine', then 'This Mac', replace the path with ${worktree}, press cmd+enter, press enter on 'Create capy', close the 'Share capy' box with escape, and then pick the project as above. Never send a message, never pick ClickVids or any other project, never leave the run selector on Cloud.

Only look, click nothing. Above the composer, the project selector must read 'capy' and the selector to its right must read this Mac (a machine name or 'This Mac'), not 'Cloud'. If both are true answer done. If the project is anything else, or the run selector reads Cloud, answer fail and say what they read.

own.goal: The model selector inside the composer (it shows a model name such as 'Claude Fable 5.1', left of the effort selector) reads 'Claude Opus 5.5', and the effort selector next to it reads 'High'. If it already does, answer done. Otherwise click the model selector, type Opus 5.5 in its search field, and click 'Claude Opus 5.5' in the Claude Code list; then set the effort to High if it is not. Change nothing else, and never send a message.

reset.jsonKeys is empty: Capy keeps model, effort and connections server-side or in localStorage, and state.json is a nested object that setJsonKeys would overwrite. reset.seeds is empty: restoreSeed throws when a seed is missing and no seed exists yet.

Updater: electron-updater in Capy sets autoDownload false, autoInstallOnAppQuit true, allowDowngrade false (main.js). A downloaded update installs at quit and changes the bundle hash, so the gate becomes stale. No setting to turn updates off was found.
